title: Scheduler slew causes attention-state fragmentation and numeric drift under hybrid-kernel routing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Under high-concurrency routing between fused attention kernels and fallback kernels, the scheduler's speculative 'slew' heuristic can cause partial state handoffs that lead to KV cache slot fragmentation and downstream numeric drift in attention outputs. Observed consequence: token-level generation divergence after ~20-40 tokens on production-like workloads and occasional deterministic softmax instability in stress tests.

Observed behavior:
- Divergence appears only on hybrid routing (fused->fallback or fallback->fused) with aggressive handoff enabled.
- Failures triggered by a combination of small batch sizes (1-4), high concurrency (>=12 request threads), and mixed precision (fp16 paths with q4 quantized fallback).
- Trace logs show out-of-order writes to adjacent KV slots and partial overwrite windows where a decoder fragment reads stale pointers.
- Numerical drift manifests as softmax probability shifts in the order of 1e-5 to 1e-3; across many tokens this cascades to different token selection.

Hypothesis / Root-cause candidates:
1) Scheduler slew reorders prefill/decode fragments so a kernel handoff can begin writing a shared KV slab while another kernel still assumes exclusive ownership, producing torn writes. Missing memory fences or non-atomic slot updates allow readers to observe partially-updated slot headers.
2) Mixed-precision fallback path uses a different packing layout for cached keys (aligned vs packed offsets), and speculative pointer translation during handoff doesn't always apply the offset fixup in the race window.
3) Rounding/quantization differences amplify tiny softmax errors when the attention numeric range is near underflow/denorm boundaries, turning minute floating differences into divergent beams.

Reproduction steps:
- Use model: redwood-v1-medium (8k context) with runtime-2.1 kernels.
- Config: routing.policy=hybrid, handoff.speculative=true, batch.size=1-4, concurrency=16, precision=fused_fp16 with fallback=q4_0.
- Run: ./tools/stress_runner --seed 2197 --threads 16 --requests 500 --prompt-set /tests/prompt_sets/consistency_small.json
- Deterministically reproduce ~2/10 runs on hardware type gtxx-rtx-A100 (or equivalent).

Logs / artifacts:
- Example log snippet (idle->handoff window):
  kernel_handshake: start decode id=0x7fae slot=0x4a12 offset=0x120
  kv_write_part: slot_header_written=true data_written=0x90 bytes=241
  kernel_preempt: preempt_to_kernel=FallbackK id=0x9fb
  kv_read: slot_header_written=false read_ok=false (observed stale header)
  softmax_debug: max_logit=12.324, max_logit_prev=12.324003 (drift 3e-6)

- Links:
  Confluence investigation doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Scheduler+Slew+State+Fragmentation+Investigation
  GitHub candidate PR (mitigations): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4882
  Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/stress_runner
  Traces and compressed logs (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-scheduler-slew-logs

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Disabled speculative handoff in dedicated-hosted (turning off routing.handoff.speculative) as of 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC; telemetry shows a drop in divergence incidents.
- Introduced an alignment-safe atomic swap for KV slot headers in the hot path (temporary patch) in branch protect/atomic-kv-header. See PR #4882.
- Added extra memory fence (platform-level) around kernel handoff sequence as a short-term guard.

Planned next steps:
- Short term (this week):
  * Complete PR #4882 code review and land atomic header swap + alignment checks (owner: Luca).
  * Extend stress harness to fuzz slot offsets and mixed-precision transitions; add nightly job.
  * Add telemetry for handoff windows: record pre-handshake timestamp, slot id, header checksum, and kernel pair; expose dashboard.
- Medium term (2-4 weeks):
  * Rework scheduler slew heuristic to include handoff-awareness: avoid reordering fragments that will touch the same KV slab within the same micro-window.
  * Add unit+integration tests that simulate torn writes and verify atomicity on all supported hardware.
  * Evaluate migrating header format to versioned atomic headers to make in-progress writes detectable and safely replayable.
- Long term:
  * Audit other shared slab usages for similar non-atomic updates and fix where necessary.
  * Investigate numeric-stability mitigations to reduce amplification of tiny discrepancies (e.g., logit clipping, denorm flushing in fallback kernels).

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- PR with atomic header swap + alignment tests merged to main and rolled to runtime-2.1-canary.
- New regression test reproduces previous divergence within CI stress job and fails before mitigation & passes after.
- Scheduler slew heuristic change in a follow-up story scheduled and scoped.

Notes / decisions so far:
- Design call 2026-03-11: agreed to land the atomic header patch as a safe, low-risk mitigation before scheduler heuristic changes. (Attendees: Maya Chen, Luca Ramirez, Priya Nair, Noah Kim)
- We will not block dedicated customers on scheduler changes; mitigations will be deployed to all tiers gradually.

Backlinks / related issues:
- ENG-314162 (follow-on: scheduler slew throttling work)
- ENG-218402 (kv slab header format v2 proposal)
